newsitem.title: CHINA: New China plant to boost synthetic ammonia output.
newsitem.headline: New China plant to boost synthetic ammonia output.

text.p: A newly expanded chemical plant in China's northwestern Gansu province will produce 300,000 tonnes of synthetic ammonia a year after beginning operations in August, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

The Lanzhou Chemical Industry Corp plant would use residual oil to produce the ammonia and would also make 520,000 tonnes of carbamide annually for grain production, the agency quoted general manager Zhu Lianbao as saying.

Gansu authorities and the China National Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) had spent more than 2.8 billion yuan ($337 million) on expanding the chemical plant, it said but gave no details of previous annual output.
Expanding an existing plant was more economical than building a new one, Zhu said.

"We imported advanced equipment and technology from Germany, the U.S., and Italy in order to enhance automation and to reduce the consumption of energy and the discharge of industrial waste," Xinhua quoted him as saying.
Chemical fertiliser use in Gansu, one of China's poorest provinces, was about 75 percent lower than the national average, it said.

The company planned to expand its ethylene output capacity to satisfy the growing demand for agriculture-related materials in northwest and southwest China, including plastic sheeting and pipes for irrigation, the agency said but did not elaborate.
